record.paper_title: On Some Open Problems in Many-Electron Theory
record.original_question: For Coulomb many-electron systems, is the ionization energy always greater than the electron affinity? Equivalently, if I[M] denotes the ionization energy of the M-electron system, is there a general proof that I[N + 1] < I[N] for Coulomb systems?

evidence.quote: To my knowledge there is no proof that the ionization energy is always greater than the electron affinity for Coulomb systems, even though this property is so very important in the study of band gaps and strong correlations. In other words, there does not appear to be a general proof that I[N + 1] < I[N] where I[M] is the ionization energy of the M-electron system.
Also, exceptions to I[N + 1] < I[N] have been found for non-Coulomb systems[6].
The property I[N + 1] < I[N] can be proven for certain Coulomb atoms.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a non-relativistic Coulomb many-electron system consisting of N electrons in the field of one or more fixed nuclei (or, more generally, an external potential consisting of a finite sum of attractive Coulomb singularities). The Hamiltonian acting on the antisymmetric subspace of L^2(R^{3N};C^2) is

  H_N = sum_{i=1}^N ( -(1/2) Δ_{x_i} + V_ext(x_i) ) + sum_{1 ≤ i < j ≤ N} 1/|x_i - x_j|,

where V_ext(x) = - sum_{k} Z_k / |x - R_k| with positive nuclear charges Z_k > 0 located at fixed positions R_k in R^3. Let E(N) denote the ground-state energy (infimum of the spectrum) of H_N restricted to fermionic wavefunctions, with E(0) := 0. Define the ionization energy of the M-electron system by

  I[M] := E(M-1) - E(M),    M ≥ 1.

The electron affinity of the N-electron system equals I[N+1] (the energy released when an extra electron is bound to the N-electron system, when binding occurs).

Prove or disprove: for every such Coulomb many-electron system, and for every N ≥ 1 for which E(N+1) is attained as an eigenvalue (i.e. the (N+1)-electron system has a bound ground state),

  I[N+1] < I[N];

equivalently, the ionization energy is strictly greater than the electron affinity.
artifact.status_search_result: No general mathematical proof of the inequality I[N+1] < I[N] (ionization energy strictly greater than electron affinity) for arbitrary Coulomb many-electron systems appears to be known. The inequality is empirically observed and can be established for certain restricted Coulomb atoms, while counterexamples exist for non-Coulomb interactions. Standard references in chemistry confirm the inequality empirically without supplying a rigorous proof.

status_evidence.title: Ionization Energy and Electron Affinity (Purdue)
status_evidence.snippet: Electron affinities are much smaller than ionization energies; the first ionization energy of sodium is roughly 1.5 times larger than the electron affinity of chlorine.
status_evidence.claim: The empirical fact that ionization energies exceed electron affinities is well documented but presented without a general proof for Coulomb systems.

status_evidence.title: On Some Open Problems in Many-Electron Theory (arXiv:1406.4475)
status_evidence.snippet: To my knowledge there is no proof that the ionization energy is always greater than the electron affinity for Coulomb systems ... exceptions to I[N+1] < I[N] have been found for non-Coulomb systems.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as an open problem in many-electron theory; only special cases have been proven.
